System design from first principles to design review

Design a parking service that can refuse the last space, survive a lost reply and recover its booking history. Trace each decision in a diagram, then inspect the rows or timings that would prove it wrong.

Start learning Browse modules

Course outline

  • From promises to a write path3 puzzles

    Estimate demand and decide who owns the last space.

    1. Can two green maps promise the last space? Define what success means before choosing storage.
    2. How much traffic arrives after a concert? Estimate peak demand and concurrent work with units.
    3. Who can grant the last space? Trace a request through two service instances and one store.
    Check what you already know
  • Data under concurrent use4 puzzles

    Protect inventory, handle retries, page history and bound staleness.

    1. How does the database choose a winner? Keep the claim and the inventory change together.
    2. What if a successful reply disappears? Recognize a retry after the database has committed.
    3. Where does the next page of history begin? Order records and handle ties before choosing an index.
    4. Why does a confirmed space still look free? Give map reads and confirmation reads explicit freshness rules.
    Check what you already know
  • Distributed work4 puzzles

    Deliver events, handle overload, move data and survive a partition.

    1. How do you send an event after a crash? Save the business change and the work it creates together.
    2. Why can retries prolong an outage? Calculate backlog growth and recovery time.
    3. When does splitting the data help? Choose a key by following the reads and writes.
    4. Who can confirm a write when regions cannot talk? Understand majority agreement and the cost of losing contact.
    Check what you already know
  • Operating and defending a design4 puzzles

    Reconcile payments, diagnose delays, recover data and defend a design under changed assumptions.

    1. What if the space expires before payment is confirmed? Make uncertain outcomes and compensation explicit.
    2. Is the database slow, or is the request waiting to reach it? Connect a user-facing objective to a concrete trace.
    3. Can you recover the right history after a bad release? Test restoration with real reads and writes.
    4. Does the design survive a changed assumption? Defend a decision, then transfer it to a different domain.
    Check what you already know
  • Operate a busy read path4 puzzles

    Route uneven work, share simultaneous cache misses and test a recovering dependency.

    1. Why does an idle worker watch a request wait? Route four reads and measure time spent waiting behind earlier work.
    2. Can two cache misses share one read? Make overlapping requests for the same reading share the work and observe how a failed read propagates.
    3. When is it worth calling a failing dependency again? Use failure replies and a quiet interval to control how many calls reach a recovering dependency.
    4. If one driver gives up, whose read should stop? Give two callers different deadlines and trace what survives the first timeout.
    Check what you already know

Final project

Defend the last seat under peak load · Design the admission and reservation paths for assigned concert seats. The reviewer will interrupt the most awkward transaction and ask which promises still hold.

How the course works

Start with the two-driver reservation. Use Run SQL to change the data in your browser, Worked code for Python 3, or Run code to compare JavaScript scenarios. The transaction lesson lets you switch between commit and rollback. Finish by defending a design for a different workload.

Every puzzle is open from this outline. The check at the end of a puzzle unlocks its next button and saves your progress in this browser.
